title: SLO Operationalization: Cross-functional Backlog & Tactical Sprint Guide
body:
Purpose:
This is a tactical guide to move SLO work from strategy into predictable execution. It focuses on: (1) a prioritized cross-functional backlog, (2) 2-week sprint-level work breakdowns for the next 8 weeks, (3) ownership and acceptance criteria templates, and (4) minimal runbook and observability integration checklists so teams can ship measurable SLOs with safe rollouts.

Context and constraints:
- Executive SLO target: 99.95% P99 availability for Hosted Inference API (non-burst endpoints) by end of Q2 2026.
- Current gaps: inconsistent measurement across regions, missing alert-to-runbook linkage, unclear owner for model-variant fallback policies, and no standardized SLO blameless postmortem template in Confluence.
- Dependencies: metrics pipeline (infra/observability), deployment routing (platform-engineering), model catalog and variants (applied-ml), Console dashboarding (product/console).

Primary goals (outcomes):
1) Ship 3 canonical SLOs for hosted inference (availability, tail latency, error budget burn) with measurement and dashboards.
2) Deploy alert → runbook → on-call flow for SLO breaches with 15-minute escalation window.
3) Establish rollout policy and safe fallback paths (model variant downgrade, regional reroute).
4) Create a repeatable template (backlog to PR) that other teams can adopt.

Stakeholders and RACI (high level):
- SRE (Maya Chen) — accountable for SLO definitions, measurement, runbooks, and on-call flow.
- Platform Engineering (Ivan Petrov) — responsible for routing, fallback primitives, and deployment hooks.
- Observability (Ethan Park) — responsible for metric collection/dashboards, alert rules, and metric-based checks.
- Applied ML (Sandra Iqbal) — consult, provide model variant compatibility matrix, and validate quality regression risk for fallback.
- Product/Console (Riley Thompson) — expose SLOs and incident summaries in Console.
- Solutions Eng / CS (Diego Morales) — customer impact advisories and external comms draft.

Backlog (prioritized epics and representative tickets):
P0 epics (must ship before next review cycle):
- EPIC: canonical-slo-metrics-pipeline (JIRA-ENG-2145) — ensure consistent metrics with tags (region, model_variant, route).
  - TASK: add route label to request latency metric (JIRA-ENG-2150)
  - TASK: export p99/p95 computations to telemetry playground (JIRA-ENG-2151)
  - TASK: cross-region aggregation job (JIRA-ENG-2160)

- EPIC: slo-alerting-and-runbook-linkage (JIRA-PROD-3180) — map alerts to runbooks and on-call play.
  - TASK: standard alert naming and tooling (JIRA-PROD-3181)
  - TASK: runbook templates in Confluence + link IDs in alert annotations (JIRA-PROD-3182)

- EPIC: fallback-routing-and-safe-degrades (PR-987) — implement programmatic model-variant fallback and region-level routing override.
  - TASK: implement routing flag for canary -> fallback (PR-991)
  - TASK: config surface for product to set customer-level fallback preferences

P1 epics (next wave):
- EPIC: console-slo-dashboard (CON-402) — Console UX for SLO status and drilldowns.
- EPIC: regression-eval-tie-in (ML-120) — ensure fallback model variants have eval pass thresholds.

Sprint plan (next 4 sprints, 2 weeks each):
Sprint 1 (Weeks 1–2): measurement and pipeline hardening
- Owner: Observability + SRE
- Goals: route-labelled metrics, p95/p99 export, proof-of-concept dashboard for one region.
- Acceptance criteria: p99 available in Metrics Playground for /v1/generate route; dashboard shows historical 30-day baseline; at least one alert defined but disabled (for testing).

Sprint 2 (Weeks 3–4): alert->runbook linkage + runbook skeletons
- Owner: SRE + Product Docs
- Goals: create runbook template, author runbooks for 'High tail latency' and 'Increased 5xx rates' for hosted-api; alerts annotated with runbook links; on-call escalation flow documented.
- Acceptance criteria: runbooks published in Confluence; alerts reference runbook IDs; dry run executed with simulated breach.

Sprint 3 (Weeks 5–6): routing fallbacks and canary safety
- Owner: Platform Engineering + Applied ML
- Goals: implement fallback route, add feature flag for rollback, ensure fallback model has eval thresholds.
- Acceptance criteria: deployment can switch to fallback within <30s in staging; fallback model passes regression checks; automated test for fallback flow added.

Sprint 4 (Weeks 7–8): Console exposure + customer-facing comms
- Owner: Product + Solutions Eng
- Goals: expose SLO status in Console, wire up customer advisory template, run tabletop with CS and SRE.
- Acceptance criteria: Console shows SLO tile for default org; advisory template exists; tabletop run and action items tracked in backlog.

Runbook skeleton (minimal required fields):
- Title
- Runbook ID (Confluence link)
- Symptoms / signal metrics (exact metric + threshold)
- Quick checks (3 bullets)
- Immediate mitigations (toggle routing, disable canary, increase replicas)
- Owner & escalation (primary, secondary, exec notify)
- Postmortem and retrospective link
- Rollback / fallback steps (exact CLI/console actions)

Observability integration checklist (must pass before alert enabled):
1) Metric has stable cardinality and labels documented.
2) P99 computed server-side and available in playground.
3) Alert annotation includes runbook link and contact.
4) PagerDuty escalation configured (test notification sent).
5) Dashboard panel passes accuracy test against raw traces for sample time window.

Acceptance criteria and measurable definitions (examples):
- Availability SLO: requests without 5xx or 429 during business-as-usual flow; SLO window 30d; burn rate alarm triggers at 2x budget burn in 1h.
- Tail latency SLO: P99 < 1.2s for small completions (<256 tokens); aggregated by region and route.
- Error budget policy: during breaches, automatic canary pause if burn rate > 5x for 30m; human-in-loop decision required for full rollback.

Open questions / risks (to be resolved in design review):
- How to measure quality impact when falling back to smaller/quantized model variants? (ML to provide delta thresholds)
- Is cross-customer routing acceptable for privacy/regulatory customers? Need policy guardrails from security/compliance.
- Cost impact of aggressive p99 smoothing vs accuracy of signal (observability team to propose compromise).

Communication plan and templates:
- Internal: weekly reliability sync summary and SLO scoreboard posted to #sre-ops and sent to Eng Leaders. Use templated subject: "SLO Update: <service> — <metric> — <status>".
- External: customer advisory template with: impact summary, timeframe, mitigation steps, next steps, customer contact. Draft owned by Solutions Eng.

Definition of Done checklist (for each SLO):
- Metric emitted with required labels
- Dashboard and alert defined (and tested in staging)
- Runbook authored and linked in alert annotation
- Fallback path defined and exercised in staging
- Console tile added (or tracked for later wave if P1)
- Post-deployment evaluation plan (30d) with quality checks

Workback calendar (high level milestones):
- 2026-02-15: Kickoff (done)
- 2026-03-05: Measurement PoC & first alerts (target)
- 2026-03-19: Runbooks & dry-run escalation (target)
- 2026-04-02: Fallbacks in staging + tests (target)
- 2026-04-16: Console and tabletop run (target)

Next steps (immediate actions this week):
- Observability: create JIRA subtasks for metric labelling (owner: Ethan)
- Platform: open PR for routing flag and add tests (owner: Ivan)
- ML: share model-variant compatibility matrix and eval thresholds (owner: Sandra)
- SRE: draft runbook template and Confluence space (owner: Maya)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally tactical: it is the "how we ship" companion to the SLO framework page. Please flag missing dependencies (e.g., legal review for cross-region routing) and suggest slot owners if you will take part in the sprint work.

Appendix (quick links & templates):
- Runbook template snippet: "Symptoms / Quick Checks / Mitigation / Rollback / Postmortem link"
- SLO definition template: "Service / SLO name / Metric / Window / Target / Burn policy / Owner / Dashboard link"
- Example alert name convention: slo.<service>.<slo_name>.breach.region

Unresolved items to capture as separate tickets:
- LEGAL-REQ: cross-region fallback policy review
- ML-REQ: automated regression test for quantized fallback models
- COST-ANALYSIS: estimate run cost for higher retention of p99 lookback

End of guide.

Revision log:
- 2026-02-15 created by Maya Chen (kickoff notes)
- 2026-02-24 updated: added prioritized epics and sprint 1 acceptance criteria (Ethan)
- 2026-03-05 updated: added sprint 3 fallback tasks and PR links (Ivan)
